en: Here, where like you're going to have, you know, folks for like the food rights or whatever it is against people for a safer future.

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, The Washington Post has reported that the big food industry is already funding body positivity pushbacks against some of this.

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, covertly, just like the cigarette companies covertly funded denial about lung cancer and just like the oil companies covertly for many decades funded global warming denial.
zh: 我是说，秘密地，就像烟草公司秘密资助关于肺癌的否认一样，就像石油公司几十年来秘密资助全球变暖的否认一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

en: I mean, I think we are, and there's going to be a huge tension there.

speaker: Unknown
en: And just the economic consequences are just, already we're seeing so many of these kind of unpredictable effects.
zh: 仅仅是经济后果就已经是，我们已经看到如此多这种不可预测的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, think about, you mentioned the food companies, the head of Nestle, Mark Schneider, has been making very nervous noises about their confectionery, Dunkin' Donuts, you know, sorry, Krispy Kreme Donuts, rather.
zh: 我是说，想想看，你提到了食品公司，雀巢的负责人 Mark Schneider 一直在对他们的甜品发出非常紧张的声音，Dunkin' 甜甜圈，你知道，抱歉，是 Krispy Kreme 甜甜圈。

en: I mean, yeah, because Ozempic goes right after their target market.

en: Exactly.
zh: 确切地。

zh: 我的两个双下巴中至少有两个是因为 Dunkin' 甜甜圈和 Krispy Kreme，现在我不再需要它了，对吧？

en: The loss of my customer loan must have caused some of that plunging stock value.
zh: 失去我这位客户肯定造成了其中的一些股票价值暴跌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and just think about the unpredictable cascading effects.
zh: 是的，只要考虑那些不可预测的级联效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jefferies Financial just did a big report about a year ago.
zh: Jefferies Financial 就在大约一年前做了一份大型报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: To the American Airlines saying you're going to have to spend a lot less money on jet fuel pretty soon because it takes so much less jet fuel to fly a radically thinner population.
zh: 致美国航空，说你很快将不得不在喷气燃料上花更少的钱，因为让一个明显更瘦的人口坐飞机飞行需要消耗的喷气燃料少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And bear in mind, this is the case now when these drugs are extraordinarily expensive in the United States.
zh: 请记住，现在是这种情况，当这些药物在美国极其昂贵的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But eight years from now, Ozempic goes out of patent.
zh: 但八年后的现在，Ozempic 专利到期。

speaker: Unknown
en: At that point, it will be a daily pill.
zh: 在那时，它将是一种每日药丸。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be a dollar a day.
zh: 它将是一天一美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the 12 big risks that I warn about in relation to these drugs don't bear out or are not super bad, then my prediction is that more than half of the population will be taking them when it's a daily pill that's a dollar a day.
zh: 如果我警告的与这些药物相关的 12 个大风险没有出现或者不是特别糟糕，那么我的预测是，当它是一天一美元的每日药丸时，超过一半的人口将服用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The effects on the economy and the society at that point are enormous.
zh: 对那时经济和社会的影响是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, my book is called Magic Pill because there's three ways these drugs can be magic, right?
zh: 你知道，我的书叫 Magic Pill，因为有三种方式这些药物可以是神奇的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is the most obvious.
zh: 第一种是最明显的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could just solve the problem, right?
zh: 它可以解决问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are days when it feels like that.
zh: 并且有些日子感觉就是那样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got to be honest with you.
zh: 我必须对你诚实。

en: My whole life I've overeaten.
zh: 我的一生都暴饮暴食。

zh: 现在，我每周一次在腿上注射我自己。

zh: 我不再暴饮暴食了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like magic.
zh: 感觉像魔法。

zh: 它可能是魔法的方式第二种更令人不安。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be like a magic trick.
zh: 它可能像是一个魔术戏法。

en: It could be like a conjurer who shows you a card trick while picking your pocket.
zh: 它可能像是一个在你给你看纸牌戏法时掏你口袋的魔术师。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be...
zh: 它可能是...

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time, the 12 big risks associated with these drugs that I describe in the book outweigh the benefits.
zh: 随着时间的推移，我在书中描述的与这些药物相关的 12 个大风险超过了益处。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do not rule that out.
zh: 我不排除那种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is perfectly conceivable.
zh: 那是完全可想象的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the third way it could be magic is to me actually the most likely.
zh: 但它可能是魔法的第三种方式对我来说实际上是最可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about the classic stories of magic that we grew up with as kids, like Aladdin, say.
zh: 如果你想想我们从小长大的经典魔法故事，比如说 Aladdin。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they go?
zh: 它们是怎么发展的？

speaker: Unknown
en: You find the lamp, you rub it, the genie appears, your wish is granted and your wish comes true, but never quite in the way you expected.
zh: 你发现了神灯，你擦它，精灵出现，你的愿望被实现，你的愿望成真，但从来不是以你预期的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's all sorts of unpredictable effects.
zh: 有各种各样的不可预测的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we can see that.
zh: 我认为我们可以看到那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them will be enormous, some of the anticipated and indeed proven positive effects are enormous.
zh: 其中一些将是巨大的，一些预期的并且确实被证实是积极的影响是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, think about effects on heart disease.
zh: 你知道，想想对心脏病的影响。

zh: 将你心脏病发作或中风的风险降低 20%，对吧？

zh: 这很可能会救我的命。

en: I'm older than my grandfather ever got to be.
zh: 我的年龄比我祖父曾经活到的岁数要大。

en: He died when he was 44 of a heart attack.
zh: 他在 44 岁时死于心脏病发作。

zh: 我家里的很多男性都有心脏问题。

zh: 我父亲有严重的心脏问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: My uncle died of a heart attack.
zh: 我叔叔死于心脏病发作。

speaker: Unknown
en: For people like us, it could be transformative.
zh: 对于像我们这样的人来说，这可能是变革性的。

zh: 在谱系的另一端，对于患有饮食失调症的人来说，我真的担心这将是致命的。

en: I can go into more detail on that if you want, but I think an opioid-like death toll of young girls who use these drugs to starve themselves is one of the reasons we need to tighten the regulation around these drugs urgently.
zh: 如果你想的话，我可以更详细地谈论这一点，但我认为，使用这些药物来让自己挨饿的年轻女孩出现类似阿片类药物的死亡人数，是我们需要紧急收紧对这些药物的监管的原因之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, we came up with the smartphone comparison, or rather the Barclays analyst did.
zh: 所以，你知道，我们提出了智能手机的比较，或者更确切地说是巴克莱分析师提出的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we'd been talking in 2007, I think it was April 2007 when Steve Jobs first unveiled the iPhone, we would not have been able to predict TikTok and Me Too and DoorDash and all these things that have transformed our lives, right?
zh: 如果我们在 2007 年谈话，我想那是 2007 年 4 月，史蒂夫·乔布斯首次发布 iPhone 时，我们无法预测 TikTok、Me Too、DoorDash 以及所有这些改变了我们生活的事情，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But here we are.
zh: 但我们到了这一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've changed our societies profoundly.
zh: 它们深刻地改变了我们的社会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think these drugs are gonna, it's not hyperbole to talk about these drugs in the same breath.
zh: 我认为这些药物会……将相提并论这些药物并非夸大其词。

en: Yeah, and I think it bears repeating.
zh: 是的，我认为这值得重复。

en: How is society, it just seems like there are powerful forces that are going to really come in opposition to this stuff.

en: And you can't say right now.
zh: 而你现在不能断言。

en: You've got the food industry and you've got pharma.
zh: 你有食品行业，还有制药行业。

zh: 所以是的，这两种力量之间肯定会有摩擦。

en: Let me talk a little bit about how we might happen, how it might happen in the short term.
zh: 让我谈谈我们可能会如何发生，或者说短期内它可能会如何发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you mentioned that 2030 is when the patent comes off of Ozempic, but actually in China, that patent's off now.
zh: 我的意思是，你提到 2030 年是 Ozempic 专利到期的时候，但在中国，专利现在就到期了。

en: And there are compounding pharmacies that are effectively putting Ozempic together on their own, sort of off-label.
zh: 有一些配制药房实际上是在自己把 Ozempic 组合起来，属于某种标签外使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they add B12 in to say, okay, it's actually something different.
zh: 也许他们会加入 B12 来说，好吧，这实际上是不同的东西。

en: And that's where lots of people are getting this drug from.
zh: 这就是很多人从那里获得这种药物的地方。

en: And the only reason that they're able to get it from these compounding pharmacies is because Ozempic right now is on some sort of shortage list, which means that they're able to get it from these supply chains.

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a chance within the next couple of years that it's going to be removed from those shortage lists.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm sure the food industry and anyone who's concerned about GDP would want it removed, even though it's not going to be good for global health.
zh: 我确信食品行业和任何关心 GDP 的人都希望它被移除，即使这不会对全球健康有利。

en: So what do you think is going to happen on that front and how impactful do you think it might be if you have, let's say, millions of people taking effectively the same drug as Ozempic and then all of a sudden it goes from an affordable drug to what it is now if you want to get it name-branded, which is $1,300 a week?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's $1,300 a month.
zh: 是每月 1300 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would just pull back for a moment.
zh: 我想先稍微退一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a really important question.
zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would just pull back for a moment and say, I guess, a few things.
zh: 我想先稍微退一步说，我想说几点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is a question of drug prices.
zh: 首先是药物价格的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you can tell from my weird Downton Abbey accent, I'm in fact British, and I spend a lot of my time in the US, a lot of my time in Britain.
zh: 你可以从我怪异的《唐顿庄园》口音听出来，我实际上是英国人，我很多时间在美国，很多时间在英国。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've got to tell you, it constantly stuns me the degree to which Americans are ripped off when it comes to drug prices.
zh: 我必须告诉你，美国人在药物价格方面被敲竹杠的程度一直让我震惊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I buy my Ozempic here in Britain.
zh: 所以我在英国买我的 Ozempic。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the equivalent of $250 a month.
zh: 这相当于每月 250 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I've had to get it in Vegas a few times, it's like $1,000 a month, right?
zh: 当我有几次在维加斯不得不买到它时，就像每月 1000 美元，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't magically transform as it crosses the Atlantic.
zh: 它在穿越大西洋时并不会神奇地转化。

speaker: Unknown
en: This happens for a reason.
zh: 这是有原因的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the United States, Big Pharma employs armies of lobbyists to rig drug regulation in the United States, right?
zh: 在美国，大型制药公司雇佣了成群的说客来操纵美国的药物监管，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: All drugs, almost without, you don't have to go so far away as Britain, just cross the Canadian border.
zh: 所有药物，几乎不……你不需要远到英国，只需越过加拿大边境。

speaker: Unknown
en: All drugs are radically more expensive in the United States than they are in Canada or Mexico, right?
zh: 所有药物在美国都比在加拿大或墨西哥贵得多，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not because the drugs are different, it's because the American political system doesn't work, it's not properly democratic, and it allows the ripping off of American citizens at every stage.
zh: 不是因为药物不同，而是因为美国政治体系不起作用，它不是适当的民主制度，它允许在每个阶段敲诈美国公民。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, both parties take massive amounts of money from Big Pharma.
zh: 顺便说一句，两党都从大型制药公司那里收取大量资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the first thing you have to say.
zh: 所以这是你必须说的第一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there's an issue around these drugs.
zh: 现在，围绕这些药物有一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the issue of the benefits of these drugs and the risks of these drugs.
zh: 存在这些药物的好处和这些药物的风险的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure we're going to dig more into that.
zh: 我肯定会我们将更深入地探讨这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't believe everyone who's overweight or obese should be taking these drugs.
zh: 而且我不相信每个超重或肥胖的人都应该服用这些药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some people who shouldn't be.
zh: 有些人是不应该服用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I hope my book is a kind of guide to so we can think this through in a very personalized way.
zh: 我希望我的书能作为一种指南，以便我们能够以非常个性化的方式思考这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a very good job with that.
zh: 那在这方面做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, thank you.
zh: 噢，谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I'd say is we're in this nightmare situation where the people who do... At the moment, only a very small elite of people can access these drugs.
zh: 但我想说的是，我们正处于这种噩梦般的境地，那些做……的人目前，只有极少数的精英阶层能够获得这些药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a situation where the real housewives of New Jersey get to be bone thin while the real schoolchildren of New Jersey get diabetic at the age...
zh: 所以我们面临这样的情况，新泽西的真实主妇们变得骨瘦如柴，而新泽西的真实学童们却在年纪轻轻时就得了糖尿病……

speaker: Unknown
en: And the number I heard is that only 2% of obese people of the obese market is on these GLP drugs, right?
zh: 我听到的数字是，只有 2% 的肥胖人群，在这个肥胖市场中，正在使用这些 GLP 药物，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: These are those epic style drugs where if you're severely overweight, 20% are doing this bariatric surgery to shrink the stomach.
zh: 这些是史诗风格的药物，如果你严重超重，20% 的人做这种减肥手术来缩小胃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, much riskier, much, much riskier.
zh: 是的，风险大得多，风险大得多的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think there's just a huge...
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为只是有一个巨大的……

speaker: Unknown
en: Huge issue around that, and so you raise compounding.
zh: 巨大的问题围绕于此，所以你提到了配制药。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for people who don't know, yeah, when a drug is, when you can demonstrate a medical need for a drug, but there is a shortage of that drug, as there is at the moment, and it's worth explaining why there's a shortage, every person who takes a Zempik, Wegovy, Manjaro becomes a walking advertisement for that drug, right?
zh: 所以对于不知道的人来说，是的，当一种药物，当你能够证明对某种药物有医疗需求，但该药物存在短缺，就像目前的情况一样，而且值得解释一下为什么会有短缺，每个服用 Zempik、Wegovy、Manjaro 的人都成为了那种药物的行走的广告，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot about a guy I interviewed called Jeff Parker, lovely guy, 67-year-old retired lighting engineer in San Francisco.
zh: 我经常想起我采访过的一个叫 Jeff Parker 的人，很好的人，67 岁的退休照明工程师，住在旧金山。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was very severely obese.
zh: 他非常严重地肥胖。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was in quite a lot of physical pain as a result.
zh: 因此他遭受着相当多的身体疼痛。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was difficult for him to walk.
zh: 他很难走路。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had gout.
zh: 他有痛风。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had liver and kidney problems.
zh: 他有肝脏和肾脏问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was taking fistfuls of pills every morning.
zh: 他每天早上都要吃一大把药。

speaker: Unknown
en: He started to take Manjaro.
zh: 他开始服用 Manjaro。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, he was getting a compounded version from China, like you say.
zh: 实际上，他就像你说的那样，从中国获得了配制的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lost an enormous amount of weight, came off all his pills, all his medical conditions went into reverse.
zh: 体重减轻了巨大幅度，停掉了所有的药，所有的医疗状况都逆转了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now he walks his dog over the Golden Gate Bridge every day.
zh: 现在他每天都会带着狗在金门大桥上散步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And said to me, I feel like I'm going to enjoy my retirement.
zh: 并对我说，我觉得我可以享受我的退休生活了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, everyone who knows Jeff looks at him and goes, whoa, what happened to Jeff, right?
zh: 现在，每个认识 Jeff 的人看到他都会说，哇，Jeff 怎么了，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: He looks completely different.
zh: 他看起来完全不同了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the reasons there's these shortages is that everyone then becomes a walking ad.
zh: 所以出现这些短缺的原因之一就是每个人随后都变成了行走的广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so demand produces demand, produces demand, produces demand in this cascading effect.
zh: 所以需求产生需求，产生需求，产生需求，产生这种级联效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So although they have been, Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, the companies that make these drugs, have been massively, to be fair to them, expanding production.
zh: 尽管他们一直，诺和诺德和礼来，这些制造这些药物的公司，一直大规模地，公平地说，在扩大生产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, they want to, they want to make the money.
zh: 当然，他们想要，他们想要赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're racing to get to a finishing line that's just getting further and further away because the more they race, the more people want it, right?
zh: 他们正在冲向一个终点线，但那个终点线正变得越来越远，因为他们越冲刺，人们就越想要它，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So lots of companies are producing compounded copies of these drugs.
zh: 所以很多公司都在生产这些药物的配制品副本。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's inherently risks in that.
zh: 这其中存在固有的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not made in FDA labs.
zh: 它们不是在 FDA 实验室制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In Austria recently, there was a big problem where people bought what they thought was compounded semaglutides, the active component of these drugs.
zh: 最近在奥地利，发生了一个大问题，人们购买了他们认为是配制的 semaglutides，这些药物的活性成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They weren't.
zh: 但实际上不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: They went into comas.
zh: 他们陷入了昏迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were horribly injured.
zh: 他们受了严重的伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an inherent risk in compounded versions for obvious reasons.
zh: 出于显而易见的原因，配制品版本存在固有的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I understand why people are doing it, right?
zh: 但我理解人们为什么这样做，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, there's a tremendous complexity.
zh: 所以是的，这里有着巨大的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you're right that big pharma will be pressuring to close those loopholes pretty soon.
zh: 我认为你是对的，大型制药公司将很快施压以关闭这些漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, they're already sending out lawyers' letters to health spas.
zh: 我的意思是，他们已经在向健康水疗中心发出律师函了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that happens, I mean, you could abruptly have people thrown off the medicine, whereas they can afford the compounded drug.
zh: 如果这种情况发生，我的意思是，你可能会突然让人们被迫停药，而他们还能负担配制的药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: They cannot afford $1,300 a month.
zh: 他们负担不起每月 1300 美元的费用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happens if you get abruptly tossed off the drug?
zh: 那么如果你突然被停药会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's a really important question.
zh: 这是一个非常重要的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to explain what the drug companies say, and I want to explain why they're probably right, but we need to take it with a small pinch of salt.
zh: 所以我想解释一下制药公司的说法，我想解释为什么他们可能是对的，但我们需要对此稍微持保留态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: What the drug companies say is these drugs are like statins or blood pressure meds.
zh: 制药公司的说法是，这些药物就像他汀类药物或降压药。

speaker: Unknown
en: They work for as long as you take them, and when you stop taking them, they stop working.
zh: 只要你服用它们，它们就有效，而当你停止服用时，它们就停止工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you regain the weight pretty rapidly.
zh: 所以你会很快恢复体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have funded a study that seems to demonstrate this.
zh: 他们资助了一项研究，似乎证明了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vast majority of people regain the vast majority of their weight within a year.
zh: 绝大多数人在一年内恢复了绝大部分体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a small pinch of salt in that, in that of course they have a vested interest in telling us that we have to take them forever because they make money forever.
zh: 这其中有一点需要保留，因为当然他们有既得利益，告诉我们必须永远服用它们，因为他们可以永远赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: There do seem anecdotally to be some people who take them for a shorter period, use them to radically change their habits, and then seem to stay at a lower weight, although I suspect they're a minority.
zh: 从轶事来看，似乎确实有一些人在较短的时间内服用它们，利用它们彻底改变习惯，然后似乎保持在较低的体重，尽管我怀疑他们是少数。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'll be more research on this soon.
zh: 不久将会有更多关于这方面的研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, if you're thrown off, you'll almost certainly regain the weight.
zh: 是的，如果你被停药，你几乎肯定会恢复体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right and that could be a very big issue as we see again these opposing forces sort of try to jockey for position here as this drug takes off.
zh: 是的，正如我们再次看到的，随着这种药物的兴起，对立力量试图争夺优势，这可能成为一个非常大的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be worse than that.
zh: 情况可能比那更糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know and there's a lot of things we don't know about these drugs.
zh: 我们不知道，而且关于这些药物有很多我们不知道的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is so we know if you gained a load of weight now and then went on a diet and lost weight and it just through calorie restriction and exercise so not using these drugs
zh: 一是，我们知道，如果你现在增加了很多体重，然后节食并减肥，这只是通过热量限制和运动，所以不使用这些药物

speaker: Unknown
en: We know that slows down your metabolism over time.
zh: 我们知道这会随着时间的推移减慢你的新陈代谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it harder to keep weight off, right?
zh: 这让你更难保持体重，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you yo-yo diet, if you gain weight, lose weight, gain weight, lose weight, it can really wreck your metabolism so you actually burn calories very slowly.
zh: 如果你反复节食，如果你增重、减肥、增重、减肥，这真的会破坏你的新陈代谢，所以你实际上燃烧卡路里的速度很慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know if taking these drugs and then coming off them slows down your metabolism.
zh: 我们不知道服用这些药物然后停药是否会减慢你的新陈代谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably does.
zh: 很可能是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most other forms of weight loss do.
zh: 大多数其他形式的减肥都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, all other forms of weight loss do.
zh: 事实上，所有其他形式的减肥都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's another concern as well.
zh: 所以这也是另一个担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you actually end up fatter than you were if you hadn't taken the drug?
zh: 如果你没有服用这种药物，你最终会不会比你原来更胖？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know, but it's a concern.
zh: 我们不知道，但这是一个担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that I found so interesting in your book was this concept of a set point that your body basically figures out the weight that you are, the weight that you should be.
zh: 我在你的书中发现非常有趣的一件事是设定点的概念，你的身体基本上会弄清楚你的体重，你应该有的体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you try to move too far off of it, at least, you know, in terms of the negative, it will try to bring you back up to that set point of weight.
zh: 如果你试图偏离它太远，至少，你知道，在负面方面，它会试图让你恢复到那个体重的设定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, this is really interesting because there's the way people used to think about this in the 60s and 70s and there's the way we understand it now.
zh: 嗯，这真的很有趣，因为人们在 60 年代和 70 年代过去思考这个问题的方式，和我们现在的理解方式之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the 60s and 70s, scientists thought that your weight was basically set from birth or even in utero, that basically from when you're born, you have a certain fat percentage that's kind of innate to you, right?
zh: 所以在 60 年代和 70 年代，科学家认为你的体重基本上是从出生时设定的，甚至在子宫里，基本上就是从你出生开始，你就有某种与生俱来的脂肪百分比，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So think about your temperature set point as an analogy.
zh: 所以把你的温度设定点作为一个类比来思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a natural set body temperature.
zh: 我们有一个自然的体温设定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go higher than that, your body works very hard to bring it down.
zh: 如果你高于那个，你的身体会非常努力地把它降下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you sweat.
zh: 它让你出汗。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you really want to get into the shade.
zh: 它让你真的想进入阴凉处。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go lower than that, your body works really hard to bring it up.
zh: 如果你低于那个，你的身体会非常努力地把它升起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you shiver.
zh: 它让你发抖。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes you seek warmth.
zh: 它让你寻找温暖。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was thought that so it's very hard to stay out.
zh: 人们认为，所以很难保持在外面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, you can't stay outside your safe temperature level, your temperature set point for very long, right?
zh: 基本上，你不能长时间保持在你的安全温度水平之外，你的温度设定点，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Your body really works to keep you there.
zh: 你的身体真的很努力地让你待在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do stay out of it for long, you get very unwell.
zh: 如果你真的在外面待太久，你会变得很不舒服。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was thought that there was something similar with your weight, that you had an innate set point that just sort of regulated.
zh: 所以人们认为你的体重也有类似的情况，你有一个天生的设定点，只是某种调节。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could go a little bit above or a little bit below, but it was basically set and regulated.
zh: 你可以稍微高一点或稍微低一点，但它基本上是设定和调节的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the obesity crisis happened, mainly starting in the early 1980s, late 70s, early 80s when I was born.
zh: 然后肥胖危机发生了，主要始于 1980 年代早期，70 年代后期，80 年代早期，我出生的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not blaming myself.
zh: 我不怪我自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not like Damien in The Omen, couldn't cause it.
zh: 我不像《凶兆》里的 Damien，不可能导致它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that seemed to blow set point theory up, right?
zh: 这似乎推翻了设定点理论，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, what's going on?
zh: 那么，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's set, if it's innate and biological,
zh: 如果它是设定的，如果是天生的和生物学的，

speaker: Unknown
en: How come it changed so much so quickly?
zh: 为什么它变化得如此之快如此之多？

speaker: Unknown
en: But what scientists realized, this is contested, but I think it's quite persuasive, is actually what happens is you do have an innate set point, but as you gain weight, your set point rises.
zh: 但科学家们意识到了，这虽然有争议，但我认为它相当有说服力，实际上发生的事情是你确实有一个固有的调定点，但随着你体重的增加，你的调定点会上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is really important for understanding why the alternative to these drugs, diet and exercise, does not produce sustained weight loss for about 85% of people who try it.
zh: 这对于理解为什么这些药物的替代方案，即节食和运动，对尝试者中约 85% 的人无法产生持久的减重效果非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say that you now gained 40 pounds.
zh: 所以假设你现在增加了 40 磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you try to lose that 40 pounds through calorie restriction and exercise.
zh: 你试图通过限制热量和运动来减掉那 40 磅。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because your innate set point has risen, your brain is trying to hold you at that higher weight.
zh: 因为你固有的调定点已经上升，你的大脑正试图把你维持在那个更高的体重上。

speaker: Unknown
en: All sorts of physical and biological changes will happen in your brain and your body to try to stop you going down.
zh: 你的大脑和身体会发生各种各样的生理和生物学变化，试图阻止你的体重下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will slow your metabolism down so you burn calories more slowly.
zh: 它会减慢你的新陈代谢，这样你燃烧热量的速度就会变慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll make you crave more sugary, salty foods.
zh: 它会让你渴望更多含糖和咸的食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: All sorts of changes happen.
zh: 发生了各种各样的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's lots of evidence for that, overwhelming evidence about metabolic slowdown, for example.
zh: 对此有很多证据，例如关于新陈代谢减慢的压倒性证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember when I first learned that, thinking, well, that can't be true.
zh: 我记得当我第一次学到这一点时，我想，这不可能是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because why, obesity is really bad for your health.
zh: 因为为什么，肥胖对你的健康真的很不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would evolution endow us with the desire to hold onto, or biological mechanisms to hold onto obesity, given that obesity is so bad for us, it's so maladaptive, it doesn't make sense to me.
zh: 为什么进化会赋予我们保留肥胖的愿望，或者保留肥胖的生物学机制，既然肥胖对我们如此不利，它是如此适应不良，这对我来说说不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was explained to me by Professor Michael Lowe, who I mentioned before at Drexel.
zh: 之前提到过的德雷塞尔大学的 Michael Lowe 教授向我解释了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best way of thinking about this, I think, which is you've got to think about the circumstances where human beings evolved.
zh: 我认为理解这一点的最好方式是你必须考虑人类进化的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the circumstances where human beings evolved,
zh: 在人类进化的环境中，

speaker: Unknown
en: The situation we live in now essentially never happened or vanishingly rarely, which is where you have...
zh: 我们现在生活的这种情况基本上从未发生过或极其罕见，也就是你有……

speaker: Unknown
en: Infinite, abundant calories all around you, far more than you could consume, and they last your whole life, right?
zh: 无限的、丰富的卡路里包围着你，远远超过你能消耗的量，并且它们持续你的一生，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That just never happened.
zh: 那从未发生过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So evolution did not prepare us for that scenario.
zh: 所以进化没有让我们为那种情况做好准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: The scenario that did happen quite frequently that evolution did prepare us for is the exact opposite, famine.
zh: 进化确实让我们做好准备的情况恰恰相反，那是饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Famine was very common, right?
zh: 饥荒是很常见的，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the circumstances where human beings evolved, it was quite likely there would be a famine in your lifetime.
zh: 在人类进化的环境中，在你的一生中很有可能发生饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about it in that context, it makes perfect sense that if you gain weight, your body fights to hold on to the weight, right?
zh: 如果你在这个背景下思考，如果你增加了体重，你的身体会努力保住体重，这是完全有道理的，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's a famine, the fattest man at the start is the last man standing, right?
zh: 如果发生饥荒，开始时最胖的人是最后幸存下来的人，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a famine.
zh: 那里有饥荒。

speaker: Unknown
en: The version of me from three years ago is going to still be alive at the end, whereas Timothee Chalamet will die in week one, right?
zh: 三年前的那个我会在最后还活着，而 Timothee Chalamet 会在第一周死掉，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll cry over his body, but he'll bury him and we'll have to move on, right?
zh: 我会为他的尸体哭泣，但他会埋葬他，我们必须继续前进，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Rest in peace.
zh: 安息吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 的确。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rest in peace, Timothee Chalamet.
zh: 安息吧，Timothee Chalamet。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 的确。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big Tim.
zh: 大 Tim。

speaker: Unknown
en: This set point, this innate set point is preparing us for a famine that now is never going to come, right?
zh: 这个调定点，这个固有的调定点正在为我们现在永远不会到来的饥荒做准备，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that explains why diets don't work.
zh: 所以这解释了为什么节食不起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also explains one theory, although this is significantly more contentious.
zh: 它也解释了一种理论，尽管这一点争议要大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a huge debate about what these drugs, so we now know these drugs are primarily working not on your gut, but on your brain.
zh: 关于这些药物有巨大的争论，所以我们现在知道这些药物主要不是在你的肠道上起作用，而是在你的大脑上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have GLP-1 receptors, not just in your gut, but in your brain.
zh: 你的 GLP-1 受体不仅仅存在于你的肠道中，也存在于你的大脑中。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're profoundly changing our brains.
zh: 它们正在深刻地改变着我们的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: From interviewing the cutting edge neuroscientists as I did for my book, this is very clear.
zh: 从我为我的书采访那些前沿的神经科学家来看，这是非常清楚的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's so disconcerting to interview the leading neuroscientists and you say to them, well, what is it doing to my brain?
zh: 采访顶尖的神经科学家是非常令人不安的，你对他们说，好吧，它对我的大脑在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they kind of go, yeah, come back and ask us in a few years, we don't really know.
zh: 他们有点像说，是啊，过几年再来问我们，我们真的不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one theory about what it may be doing to the brain is it may be lowering your biological set point.
zh: 但是关于它可能对大脑做什么的一种理论是它可能正在降低你的生物调定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The equivalent of, this is a very crude analogy, I suspect the scientists I interviewed would think it was overly crude, but it's a bit like taking your set point, resetting your iPhone to the factory settings, right?
zh: 相当于，这是一个非常粗糙的类比，我怀疑我采访的科学家会认为这过于粗糙了，但这有点像是拿你的调定点，把你的 iPhone 重置为出厂设置，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It lowers your set point for the duration that you take the drugs.
zh: 在你服用药物的期间，它会降低你的调定点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, you see, the debate about what causes obesity is intimately related to the debate about how these drugs work in all sorts of fascinating ways.
zh: 所以再次，你看，关于肥胖原因的争论与关于这些药物如何运作的争论在所有这些迷人的方式上有着密切的联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you mentioned brain chemistry.
zh: 你提到了大脑化学反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that I definitely want to talk about.
